pass_b_english: …Not knowing the Master of all, they would not have cried out to Him.

Just as Abel's blood is said to have cried out to God, and not the blood itself having a voice, but rather the atrocity of the deed disturbing God; similarly, one might think that those who are accustomed to worshiping unclean demons might cry out in a similar way, even if they do not know the God of all.
For even if they do not know the God of all, they have been oppressed by Satan, and in some way they cry out against their oppressors, requesting help through the manner of the deed.

Thus, we say that the Egyptians cried out to God because of those who oppressed them—that is, those they had made with their own hands, and who had subjected them to a most bitter slavery, clearly the unclean demons.
But the Lord will send a man to save them.
And who is this man, but clearly Christ? That is, the only-begotten Word of God appearing in human form.
He saved not only the Egyptians, but the whole earth.
He saved by judging; and what is this judging? It is to bring a just judgment upon them.
For He handed over Satan, who had plundered them, along with the unclean demons by assuming righteous votes, to be kept in chains of darkness for the judgment of the great day.

But those whom He saved after they had undergone such unbearable oppression, He also delivered, making them His own worshipers by turning to them the light of truth and surrounding them with the garments of freedom.
Thus also the Savior says: 'Now is the judgment of this world. Now the ruler of this world will be cast out. And I, if I am lifted up, will draw all to myself' (John 12:31-34).
You see that He has judged the world, having cast out Satan, who formerly tyrannized it, and having drawn all to Himself.
For even the Egyptians have come to know Him.
And indeed, having come to know Him, they make sacrifices, they offer prayers, and they fulfill their promises.
For this is what is sung through the voice of David: 'You have vowed and will repay to the Lord our God' (Psalm 50:14).
See, then, the newness of things.

For those who formerly used to sacrifice to demons, offering their services to Satan and presenting thank offerings and fulfilling their vows—even prayers and promises—having been enlightened in their mind through Christ and illuminated by the doctrines of truth, they have fled from their ancient error.

Having come to know once for all the Creator and Lord of all, they offer to Him a service in the spirit, fulfilling pure prayers and offering sacrifices, not those through blood and the slaughter of animals.
